meta.tagline: An opinionated guide to the software we use, trial, explore and question
meta.how_to_nominate: Email the IT lead with the tool, what you used it for and how it went.

blips.name: QuickBooks
blips.description: QuickBooks is our general ledger, payables and receivables for the single legal entity. Adopt: used daily for three years with a named owner and tested monthly backups. Watch-out: fund reporting needs manual spreadsheets. Keep as the ledger of record and review fund accounting options at contract renewal.

blips.name: Odoo POS
blips.description: Odoo POS is being piloted in the museum shop for stock and till sales. Trial: two months in one site with sales reconciled weekly. Watch-out: card terminal integration needs staff training. Expand to the cafe once offline mode is tested.

blips.name: Neon One
blips.description: Neon One manages memberships, renewals and donor records. Adopt: it is the single record for members with automatic renewals. Watch-out: reports are limited. Use it as the default for any new member programme.

blips.name: CiviCRM
blips.description: CiviCRM is being explored as an open source alternative to our paid member and donor database. Assess: only a demo instance exists with no live data. Next step: a data-migration proof of concept and a hosting cost estimate.

blips.name: Zendesk
blips.description: Zendesk is used for IT requests only by two staff. Hold: licence cost is high for the usage and a bundled helpdesk is available in Microsoft 365. Freeze new use and plan migration of the knowledge base before renewal.

blips.name: Microsoft 365
blips.description: Microsoft 365 provides email, files, chat and meetings for all staff. Adopt: company-wide for four years with MFA enforced. Watch-out: sharing settings are too open. Default for collaboration; review external sharing quarterly.

blips.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
blips.description: Defender for Endpoint is deployed to 20 of 60 laptops. Trial: pilot with weekly alert review by the IT lead. Watch-out: alerts need triage time. Expand to all laptops after the pilot report in Q1.

blips.name: Microsoft Copilot
blips.description: Microsoft Copilot is being evaluated for drafting and meeting summaries. Assess: five volunteers testing with no sensitive data allowed. Next step: agree a data-handling policy and measure time saved before any wider purchase.

themes.title: Fewer tools, clearer owners
body: Across the interviews the same pattern kept appearing: we pay for several tools that overlap. [[Zendesk]] is used by two people while [[Microsoft 365]] already offers a helpdesk, so we now advise against starting anything new in it.

The tools we trust most all have a named owner and a tested backup, which is why [[QuickBooks]] and [[Neon One]] sit in Adopt. We expect to apply that same bar to every Trial item before the next review.

themes.title: Open source on the horizon
body: Two open source options, [[CiviCRM]] and [[Odoo POS]], moved onto the radar this edition. Neither is proven here yet, but both could reduce licence cost, so we will watch hosting and support effort closely.
In the coming months we may see a real migration proof of concept for CiviCRM.

themes.title: Careful steps with AI and security
body: We are protecting laptops first with [[Microsoft Defender for Endpoint]], and exploring [[Microsoft Copilot]] only with non-sensitive data. We caution against wider AI use until a data-handling policy exists.

actions.action: Migrate IT knowledge base off Zendesk
